title: My Favourite Place
description: Practise relative clauses and the present perfect, then write a magazine article about a place you love.
instructions: Do the exercises in Part 1. Then write your text in Part 2.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: This is the park ___ I learned to ride a bike.
exercises.explanation: Use "where" to talk about a place: the park where I learned to ride a bike.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence with "for" or "since".
exercises.text: I have been going there ___ I was six years old.
answers: since
exercises.explanation: Use "since" with a starting point in time (since I was six) and "for" with a period of time (for ten years).

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
answers: Have you ever been to the seaside?
exercises.explanation: In present perfect questions, "have" comes before the subject and "ever" comes before the past participle: Have you ever been ...?

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: My grandmother, who she lives near the lake, often takes me there.
answers: My grandmother, who lives near the lake, often takes me there.
exercises.explanation: "Who" replaces the subject, so do not repeat it with "she": who lives, not who she lives.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: It is the ___ place I know.
exercises.explanation: Long adjectives form the superlative with "the most": the most peaceful.

exercises.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.text: Last summer I ___ (spend) every afternoon there.
answers: spent
exercises.explanation: Use the past simple with a finished time like "last summer". "Spend" is irregular: spent.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence with one linking word.
exercises.text: ___ the cafe is small, it has the best views in town.
answers: although
though
even though
exercises.explanation: "Although" (or "though") at the start of a sentence introduces a contrast with the main clause.

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word FOR. Begin: "I ..."
exercises.text: I started going to this library three years ago.
answers: I have been going to this library for three years.
I have gone to this library for three years.
I've been going to this library for three years.
I've gone to this library for three years.
exercises.explanation: An action that started in the past and continues now uses the present perfect (continuous) + for + a period of time.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: When I was younger, I ___ go there with my grandparents every Sunday.
exercises.explanation: Use "used to + infinitive" for past habits that don't happen now.

exercises.prompt: Write the correct form of the word in brackets.
exercises.text: The view from the hill is absolutely ___ (beauty).
answers: beautiful
exercises.explanation: We need an adjective after "is". The adjective from "beauty" is "beautiful" (y changes to i).

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
answers: Everyone should visit this place.
exercises.explanation: Use "should + infinitive" to recommend something.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: I enjoy to watch the boats on the lake.
answers: I enjoy watching the boats on the lake.
exercises.explanation: "Enjoy" is followed by the -ing form, not the to-infinitive: enjoy watching.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: In summer the beach is much ___ than in winter.
exercises.explanation: Two-syllable adjectives ending in -y change to -ier: busy - busier.

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word ENOUGH. Begin: "The park isn't ..."
exercises.text: The park is too small for a football match.
answers: The park isn't big enough for a football match.
The park isn't large enough for a football match.
exercises.explanation: "Too + adjective" can be changed to "not + opposite adjective + enough": too small = not big enough.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: The park is very quiet. ___, it's a great place to study.
exercises.explanation: "As a result" introduces a consequence: it is quiet, so it is good for studying.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: It is the most quiet place in the town.
answers: It is the quietest place in the town.
It is the quietest place in town.
exercises.explanation: Short adjectives take -est in the superlative, not "the most": quiet - the quietest.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
answers: I grew up near this beach.
exercises.explanation: "Grow up" means to change from a child to an adult. The past form is "grew up".

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: If you will visit my town, I will take you there.
answers: If you visit my town, I will take you there.
exercises.explanation: In the first conditional, use the present simple after "if", not "will".

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word NEVER. Begin: "I have ..."
exercises.text: This is the most peaceful place I've ever visited.
answers: I have never visited a more peaceful place.
I have never been to a more peaceful place.
I have never visited a more peaceful place than this.
I have never been to a more peaceful place than this.
I have never visited a more peaceful place than this one.
I have never been to a more peaceful place than this one.
exercises.explanation: "The most ... I have ever visited" means "I have never visited a more ... place".

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word USED. Begin: "There ..."
exercises.text: There was a cinema here, but it closed years ago.
answers: There used to be a cinema here.
exercises.explanation: "There used to be" describes something that existed in the past but doesn't now.

task.prompt: You see this notice in an English-language magazine for teenagers: "My favourite place - tell us about a place you love. Where is it? Why is it special to you?" Write your article.
contentPoints: Give your article an interesting title.
Say where the place is and describe what it looks like.
Say what you do there and how often you go.
Explain why the place is special to you.
usefulLanguage: What I love most about it is ...
If you ever visit ..., you should ...
task.modelAnswer:
A Secret Garden in the City

Have you ever wanted to escape from the noise of the city? I have the perfect place for you. It's a small garden behind the old library in my town, and very few people know about it.

The garden has tall trees, a little pond with goldfish and a wooden bench where you can sit in the shade. I've been going there since I was twelve. I usually go on Saturday mornings, when it is quiet, and I read or just listen to the birds.

What I love most about it is the feeling of calm. When I'm stressed about exams, I go there for an hour and I always feel better afterwards. In addition, it reminds me of my grandfather, who first took me there.

If you ever visit my town, you should definitely find it!
